10/20/2026
Handler approached front kennel. dog retreated to back. Handler lowered guillotine and reappraoched back. Dog was pacing back wall of kennel near guillotine. Handler offered a few treats and dog took them. When introducing the leash dog, dog began attempts to climb up kennel walls. Neighboring dogs had grown in intensity with reactivity and barking. Handler locked neighboring dogs on opposite side while attempting to leash. Handler continued to offer treats, dog would take some but not others. Handler was able to cast leash over head and secure on first attempt. Handler then opened gate wide and allowed dog to exit, dog stepped front 2 feet outside and then retreated back to kennel. Handler tried to treat lure and verbally coax dog would not exit. Handler spent about 10 minutes attempting to get dog to exit kennel. If dog pulled back and tension was created on leash (just a taut leash) dog would begin chewing on leash. Handler was able to get dog to eat treats from hand. Handler attempted several times to coax dog out of kennel but dog continued to chew on leash or attempt to scale wall (Unsuccessful). Dog had chewed half way through leash when handler ended evaluation. Handler was able to introduce leash removal tool and use tool to remove leash. When handler lifted guillotine dog began pacing between kennels with rounded posture and ears pinned back.
10/19/2026
Dog was at back of kennel, low growl, wide eyes, pacing in place, would not come forward, handler closed divider and dog startled. Handler approached back dog sniffed them through door, wide eyes, alert, low tail, weight shifted back. Handler tossed treats and dog ate them readily, handler held out leash, dog sniffed it, backing away, avoidant and lowering head away from it, handler would toss treats and attempt to place leash as dog ate, dog would flinch and back away, would come forward to stick nose out of kennel when leash was removed, but dart away when handler reached in. Eventually handler was able to drape leash over head as dog ate treats on ground, dog sat in back kennel of corner, hesitant to exit, handler tossed treats, dog pacing in kennel, leaning over threshold, would startle at nearby dogs barking and retreat back into kennel. Handler kept tossing treats and spoke softly, eventually dog slowly exited kennel with lowered posture then darting to the end of the leash, walked outside with mild pull, ears back, alert, handler tried to walk dog into the yard, dog began to thrash backwards, mouthing at leash, handler walked back with dog until they stopped, tried to walk dog to a closer yard, dog again began thrashing backwards and chewing at leash until pressure released, dog walked back to door to kennel building, sitting in corner by doorway, handler grabbed a nearby bucket and tipped it down in front of dog, dog stepped front paws into bucket but then backed out, laid down in corner, handler moved bucket away, dog sat up, handler muzzle wrapped and carried dog into yard. Once in yard, dog sprinted along fence line, tense, low tail, came back to front corner of yard and began jumping up at fence, handler slowly approached and dog stopped jumping, frozen in place, wide eyes, closed mouth, handler knelt nearby and tossed treats, dog did not engage, handler would back away, walking around yard, dog would watch them, no movement or reaction. Handler spent a few minutes in yard, dog did not move once, handler approached and dog took a small step back, rounded posture, handler picked up leash and added clip, dog followed handler out of yard, briefly thrashing back on leash but entered building easily and walked back to kennel, entered quickly and allowed leash removal with clip leash.

Dog met handler at outside gate with soft face and body, wagging tail. Attempted to push out of kennel, contained with pressure against gate, able to be leashed over top of head. Dog exited kennel, hackles raised when passing reactive dogs, this dog would begin chuffing and attempt to pull towards them. Handler used moderate leash pressure and verbal cues to guide dog away. Walked to high-yard fence. Dog explored yard, sniffing, not interested in handler but would occasionally look up and wag tail when called. Eagerly accepted treats. Allowed petting but did not seek it out. Continued to explore, began pacing at fence when hearing nearby dogs begin barking. Handler approached, dog allowed petting and leash retrieval. Moderate pull on return. Dog would growl, whine, and attempt to dart towards other dogs in kennels, needed leash pressure and coaxing to redirect. At kennel, dog initially stepped front feet inside, then quickly backed out, began fence fighting with neighboring dog. Handler walked dog away, then back, dog would not enter kennel, jumped back and attempted to run on leash. Lunged back towards neighboring dog, fence fighting. Handler guided dog away; dog turned quickly towards handler; handler straight-armed leash and walked dog away. Dog began to settle, wagged tail, allowed petting. Second handler arrived, tried luring dog into kennel; dog entered, then bolted out, resumed fence fighting. Second handler closed neighboring dogs inside, then called out to this dog through open divider. Dog entered kennel, turned and attempted to bolt as gate was being closed. These behaviors are often a response to the overwhelming sights, sounds, and confinement, along with the lack of choice or control over their environment. Although this dog continues to show appropriate behavior outside of the kennel with positive interactions with staff and volunteers, without intervention, well-being will continue to decline. Immediate placement is needed with an experienced adopter or New Hope Partner who can provide time and space to decompress in a calm, supportive home. Placement needed by close of business 11/1/26. sections.evaluation_comments:
10/27/2026
Updating color due to NHO status.
10/20/2026
Responding to loose dog call on radio* Dog was standing up alongside fence with eyes wide, ears alert, wary of ACT staff member placing leash while heavily panting, pawing towards leash to push away, allowed handler to slowly approach and place leash over head. Became erratic on leash, zig zag walking pattern, strong pull back to kennel, began thrashing/pulling on leash when approaching kennel, able to guide dog into kennel as dog thrashed with no issues, tense bodied while sitting in middle of kennel, would not come forward as handler knelt down attempting to coax over, would allow handler to slowly approach and place clip leash while in kennel, able to exit kennel and remove leash via clip leash with no issues.
10/20/2026
Dog was being leashed to be moved into the indoor part of the kennel for daily cleanig procedures, once the leash was placed the dog began to thrash and leash bite. The dog redirected up towards the handlers hand making contact and not engaging further. Upon redirection the leash became loose around the dog's neck leading the dog to stick it's paw in the loop to loosen it further and escaping the leash and kennel. The dog ran from I building over to a gate next to F building where the handler eventually caught up to the dog and an EET staff member was able to leash the dog and guide them back to kennel without issue.
10/18/2026
Presented leash, dog would start to dodge leash placement.  Able to step into kennel & leash dog.  Would walked to PY with a stop & go style on leash while needing verbal coaxing.  Once in PY, dog would explore with a relaxed & wiggly body.  Approaching handler on own & when called over.  Would "SIT" for treats & take treats gently.  Would run & do zoomies then approach handler & jump up while leaning against handlers body for more petting, able to direct off without issues.  Picked up leash & verbally coaxed dog to walk into behavior taxi without issues for kennel return.  Rode well back to kennel.  Exited into kennel & allowed leash removal to be done by hand.
Interested parties should be counseled on providing this dog with proper decompression time in a new home.  Allowing time to adjust is important for their comfort and well-being.  Adopters should be counseled on proper dog-to-dog introductions, which should only occur after the dog has fully decompressed.
*This dog may need a behavior taxi to help with an easier kennel return*
10/17/2026
Closed outside for AM cleaning. Dog approached handler with soft body and wagging tail, took treats. Avoidant of leash placement, handler stepped into kennel, dog approached, able to slowly place leash, dog exited kennel then thrashed head briefly when feeling leash pressure, quickly settled and walked with light pull to yard, ignored kenneled dogs in passing. Affiliative with handler, front paws on lap soliciting attention, leaned into handler and allowed petting all over, panting, eyes soft, tongue lolled, explored yard but checked in with handler frequently soliciting more attention. Picked up leash and walked back to kennel, once in front of kennel dog stopped and began pulling away from handler, gave dog a moment to settle, dog stood with front paws against handler, panting, body soft, tail wagging, allowed handler to pick up and carry into kennel, able to reach in and remove leash by hand.
10/16/2026
During AM cleaning dog refused to move inside with verbal coaxing and treats, dog was laying agianst back kennel door and rerfused to move, went to back side and dog got up excited to exit kennel, would dodge attempts to leash, did a big loop and got leash on, opened kennel door and dog came out, allowed petting and walked polietly to other side of building, before entering building decided to use a back clip for easy return, dog remained calm with a soft body when attatching back clip leaning against handlers legs, entering the door way the dog walked forward and hit the end of the leash, the dog whipped backwards and vocalized, handler used leash pressure away to prevent from coming towards handler and dog began biting at leash, handler quickly opened the kennel door and allowed dog to move into kennel, dog would continue to bite at leash, once in kennel dog would vocalize at any slight pressure added so quickly removed leash with back clip, once leash was removed dog went and laid down in back of kennel. Offered treats once door was closed and dog came up and ate the ones tossed on the floor after a minute.
10/16/2026
Assisted with M&G. Adoptions staff had dog on leash on approach; dog had soft body language, wagging tail, leaned into handler's legs to seek attention. Some hesitation to walk on leash but easy to encourage forward with verbal coaxing. In yard, dog greeted customer with loose body language. Dog allowed all petting, sought attention. Handler took leash for return. Dog walked well, then stopped at open kennel gate. Dog began thrashing and crying out when any leash pressure was applied. Dog would twist body, jump up into air, then land on ground. Handler released all leash tension, spoke softly, was able to pet dog. Dog softened towards handler and adoptions staff. Ate wet food from hand but would not enter kennel for it. Dog continued to thrash, twist, and cry out when handler tried guiding dog into kennel. Second handler arrived, used sort board to guide dog forward. Dog fought against leash, began chewing it, whipped body around. Handler used straight arm on leash while closing gate. Dog continued to chew on leash. Handler spoke softly, dog dropped leash, came forward, panting but appearing to settle. Dog allowed slow leash removal by hand.
10/12/2026
Nervous, tense body, skin crawling, slow leash placement, tolerated some handling and vaccine booster with muzzle wrap restraint, thrashed slightly during restraint, slowly coaxed back into kennel with slight leash pressure, clip lead used to remove leash.
10/7/2026
Solicited attentions, Playful, Moderate to pull from kennel, Easy to return to kennel, Takes treats nicely, Easy/Loose Leash, Stop and go, Calm, Sit, Stepped into kennel to leash, some stopping when dogs were barking at him, appears potty trained, food motivated, affectionate, greets staff, friendly, good boy.
10/2/2026
Soft body, wagging tail, paws up on gate to solicit attention from handler. Placing YELLOW level based on kennel presence and intake notes.
*Dog should not be introduced to any other pets until end of 14-day decompression period. Potential adopters should be counseled on proper dog introductions, which must be slow and supervised. This approach is essential for the safety, comfort, and well-being of all pets involved.*

10/25/2026
Handler approached kennel front, dog was locked in front kennel with kennel mate for AM cleaning. Handler was able to separate dog from kennel mate using guillotine and high value treats (Hotdogs). Handler reapproached front kennel and began offering treats to dog. Dog was hesitant initially, displaying rounded posture and furrowed brow. Handler was able to get dog to eat from hand withing a few minutes. Handler then draped leash on floor on kennel, dog was highly avoidant of leash. Handler placed a jackpot of treats on leash and closed gate. Dog ate all the treats after about a minute. Handler then retrieved leash and lifted guillotine. Dog retreated to the back and kennel mate came forward, handler again lowered. Dog was now in smaller portion of kennel. Handler reapproached back and tried for a few minutes to lure dogs head into leash loop. Dog was too avoidant if leash was involved. Handler was able to reach in and drape large loop overhead and secure. Dog immediately began chewing on leash. Handler opened gate and reintroduced kennel mate. Dog stopped chewing and softened slightly. Kennel mate was soft postured and affiliative during entire evaluation. Handler spent about 5-7 minutes hand feeding treats to both dogs. Dog would chew on leash as soon as tension was created, usually by kennel mate getting wrapped up in leash or stepping on leash. Handler was able to snag dogs attention most of the time and chewing stopped. Dog had by now chewed about halfway through leash. Handler decided to end evaluation. Handler was able to hand feed dog a few times and attempted to lure forward with kennel mate and remove leash by hand, but dog would not allow. Handler left leash on dog and returned both dogs to the front kennel for cleaning to continue.
10/25/2026
Handler returned to kennel about 20 minutes after evaluation, dog had chewed through leash that was left on.
10/24/2026
Dog had tense body, tucked tail, weight shifted back, retreated to back of kennel as handler approached, assistant went to other side to attempt to separate from kennel mate, both dogs would pace back and forth across divider together, eventually this dog came forward alone, ears back, wide eyes, uneasy, assistant closed divider, dog stayed toward back of kennel as handler reached in leash. Dog paced along back of kennel, avoidant of leash, tightly closed mouth, rounded posture, ducking away if handler swung leash toward her. Dog sat in back corner of kennel, low growled, handler swung leash toward dog and she grabbed it, chewing on leash, handler would gently pull at leash but dog continued to chew until leash broke. Handler went to get a second leash, reset, continued to try and gently lasso leash, dog would whip head toward leash with open mouth or duck away with each attempt. Handler opened divider and let dog through to back of kennel for smaller space, closed divider. Dog was at kennel door as handler opened it, backing away as leash was presented, pacing back and forth in kennel as handler attempted to leash. Handler managed to drape leash over head but as they tightened loop dog quickly grabbed it, chewing at leash again, handler tossed treats, dog would not be distracted, handler tried placing a towel over dog, pet along side, dog shifted away from touch, kept chewing, tried to walk out of kennel but handler closed door since leash was close to breaking. Handler kept tossing treats, dog eventually chewed through leash, handler ended evaluation.

Dog was at front of kennel, alert posture and soft face, ears up. Took treats gently. Handler cracked gate, dog pushed snout against it, eager to exit, no issues leashing. Exited quickly, strong pull to door. Once outside, dog was slightly erratic on leash, wagging tail, soft body. Dog would walk, then stop and sit against handler's legs while looking up. Second handler called dog forward, dog bounded to second handler, leaned in for petting. Some more stop and go to lean against handler but able to be directed with leash guidance. Took to main yard without issue, adjusted stopper, dropped leash. Dog explored yard with loose body language, frequently approached handlers, leaned in, allowed all petting. Demonstrated "sit" command, took treats gently. Briefly jumped up against handler for attention, could be directed down. Dog was interested in other dogs walking outside of yard; this dog would approach fence with perked ears, forward posture, broke focus when called by handlers. Dog leaned in for more petting. Briefly nibbled on handler's jacket sleeve, stopped on own, did not repeat. Light pull on return, some zig-zag. Entered kennel quickly, leash loosened via clip lead then removed fully by hand.
10/20/2026
Per PHX PD, both dogs were charging and chasing people, bit a homeless person but he left so no info on bite. They jumped up on another citizen and tore her shirt.

10/28/2026
10/28/26 12:18 This dog has started showing declining behaviors in shelter and demonstrated a recurring pattern of fluctuating in-kennel stress and anxiety, ranging from moderate to significant, over an extended period of time. These behaviors are often a response to the overwhelming sights, sounds, and confinement, along with the lack of choice or control over their environment. Although this dog continues to show appropriate behavior outside of the kennel with positive interactions with staff and volunteers, without intervention, well-being will continue to decline. Immediate placement is needed with an experienced adopter or New Hope Partner who can provide time and space to decompress in a calm, supportive home. Placement needed by close of business 11/2/26. May be at risk of euthanasia 11/3/26 or sooner if warranted.

NOT AROUND ANY CHILDREN WITH SOURCE.  PET TOLERATED LEASH PLACEMENT BUT DID TRY TO PULL BACK.  PET DID SETTLE IN CAR.  PET PULLED HARD TOWARDS, BARKING AND YIPPING WHEN STAFF APPROCHED.

10/28/2026
10/28/26 12:21 This dog has demonstrated a persistent, recurring pattern of fluctuating in-kennel stress and anxiety, ranging from moderate to significant, over an extended period of time. These behaviors are often a response to the overwhelming sights, sounds, and confinement, along with the lack of choice or control over their environment. Although this dog continues to show appropriate behavior outside of the kennel with positive interactions with staff and volunteers, without intervention, well-being will continue to decline. Immediate placement is needed with an experienced adopter or New Hope Partner who can provide time and space to decompress in a calm, supportive home. Placement needed by close of business 11/2/26. May be at risk of euthanasia 11/3/26 or sooner if warranted.
